summary: The Crohn's Disease Activity Index (CDAI) calculator turns the current weight, number of liquid stools and the complaints into CDAI score. It suits an informed starting point to take to a clinician, not a diagnosis. The unit chips sit next to the boxes, which is where most hand-calculation mistakes start.

sections.title: How does the Crohn's Disease Activity Index (CDAI) calculator work?
sections.html:
The Crohn's Disease Activity Index (CDAI) calculator takes the values in the form, applies the relationship described below and reports CDAI score in the results panel.

Working from the top of the form: you choose the option that describes your case (the sex, the abdominal pain and the overall well-being); then you type in the current weight, number of liquid stools (last 7 days), the complaints and the current hematocrit.

Press Calculate and the page works through the equation with the values you supplied and derives the rest; it then keeps up with you as you correct a typo.

Because the equation can be rearranged for each of its variables, the page also runs backwards. Leave the box you want to know empty, fill in the rest, and it solves for the missing one instead. That is useful when you know the answer you need rather than the inputs you have.

sections.title: The formula behind the Crohn's Disease Activity Index (CDAI) calculator
sections.html:
The page rests on a handful of relationships. Each one can be rearranged for any of its variables, which is what makes the calculator work in both directions:

CDAI score=(20 × complaints + 30 × drugs + 10 × abdominal mass + 35 × abdominal pain + 2 × number of liquid stools (last 7 days) + weight + 49 × overall well-being + 6 × (current hematocrit, sex))
Ideal weight=-100 × current weight ÷ (weight − 100)
Iritis=-arthritis + complaints − erythema − fever − fistula − other
Hematocrit=(current hematocrit, sex)

Read it as an ordinary equation. Where a word appears instead of a letter, it is the label of one of the boxes in the form; where a function appears, it is the usual mathematical meaning of that function.

sections.title: How are units and precision handled?
sections.html:
Units are handled by conversion rather than by convention. Whatever chip you choose, the number is turned into a single base unit before the calculation and rendered back afterwards, so a form filled with a mixture of systems still gives the right answer.

  • Mass, opening in kilograms
  • Mass, opening in kilograms

Display rounding is separate from calculation rounding: the digits you see are shortened, the value behind them is not. Numbers far from everyday size are shown in scientific notation so the significant digits stay readable.

sections.title: When should you use it?
sections.html:
The Crohn's Disease Activity Index (CDAI) calculator earns its place in the middle of a task, not instead of one. It is most useful when:

  • Deciding whether a reading is worth a second look
  • Preparing for an appointment so you can describe your numbers clearly
  • Tracking a measurement over time and understanding what changed
  • Any time the same 3 figures keep coming back — the current weight, number of liquid stools and the complaints — and you would rather not repeat the arithmetic by hand each time.

sections.title: How do you get a reliable answer?
sections.html:
• Round only at the end. The calculator carries full precision internally, so re-entering a value you already rounded is the fastest way to introduce drift.
  • Keep the units you enter consistent. Mixing centimetres into a field that expects metres is the single most common way to get an answer that is out by a factor of a hundred.
  • Change one input at a time when you are exploring. Two simultaneous changes make it impossible to tell which one moved the result.
  • Leave the field you want solved for empty rather than guessing at it. Filling every box tells the calculator you already know the answer.

sections.title: What else is worth knowing?
sections.html:
• Filling in more than one box is fine. The most recently edited field is the one treated as known, so you can switch direction without reloading.
  • Answers that depend on a drop-down reflect the option you picked, not a range. Switching to a neighbouring option is the quickest way to see how much that factor matters.
  • Some options are backed by reference tables that ship with the page, so the values are fixed data rather than a live lookup.
  • Fields that are still blank are exactly the ones the calculator has not yet been given, so the results panel is a reliable map of what is missing.

faq.q: What does the Crohn's Disease Activity Index (CDAI) calculator work out?
faq.a: It returns CDAI score, derived from the current weight, number of liquid stools and the complaints. Every field in the form feeds the same relationship: press Calculate once and changing any of them updates the result immediately, with no page reload.

faq.q: What do I need to enter to use the Crohn's Disease Activity Index (CDAI) calculator?
faq.a: The form asks for the current weight, number of liquid stools and the complaints, which is 15 fields in total. Each one is labelled with what it means and, where relevant, the unit it expects. Anything you leave blank is treated as the value to solve for.

faq.q: Can I enter current weight in a different unit?
faq.a: Yes. Current weight opens in kilograms and the chip beside it offers 29 units. The number you typed keeps its magnitude and only its label changes; the calculation itself happens in a common base unit, so mixing systems in one form is safe.
Yes. Each variable in the relationship can be the one being solved for: fill in the answer you are aiming at, leave the field you want empty, and the calculator inverts the equation for you.

faq.q: How much do the drop-down choices change the answer?
faq.a: There are several choices to make (11 in total), and each one selects a different case rather than scaling the result. Switching a single option and watching the result is the fastest way to see how much that choice is worth.

With the values the page starts from, the calculator reports Complaints = 0. Treat that as a reference point rather than a recommendation: it exists so you can tell at a glance whether your own inputs are on the same scale.

faq.q: Is the Crohn's Disease Activity Index (CDAI) calculator free to use?
faq.a: Yes — no account, no sign-up and no limit on how many times you run it. The arithmetic happens in your browser, so the values you type are not sent anywhere.
